title: SRE skill acceleration and interview sprint playbook (Platform hires) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This living playbook combines a short hiring plan, interview rubric, and an aggressive first-10-days onboarding checklist for mid-senior SRE/platform engineer hires. Intended for people-ops + eng-sre partners running a 4-week sourcing -> offer sprint and a tightly-scoped 10-day ramp for initial impact.

High-level goals:
- Hire 2 L4/L5 Platform SREs focused on inference serving reliability by EOY Q4 2025.
- Reduce mean time to first deploy from new hire from 21 days -> <= 10 days (measured by first merged PR touching infra).
- Validate candidate fit for production incident leadership, infra-as-code, and observability-first debugging.

Hiring plan snapshot (4-week sprint):
Week 0: role spec final, sourcing brief, hiring committee confirmed.
Week 1: active sourcing (LinkedIn Recruiter, H1, referrals), screen 15 candidates, schedule 8 onsites.
Week 2: interview loop (see schedule), move 3 -> take-home OR work simulation.
Week 3: debrief, reference checks, compensation calibration, extend 2 offers (1 primary + 1 fallback).

Open questions / decisions (TODO):
- Do we require a day-long in-person loop for final on-site or is hybrid acceptable? (ENG/SRE preference: hybrid).
- Take-home length: short infra-tuning lab (3hrs) vs longer project (8hrs). Recommend 3hrs.

Interview loop: Purpose-driven rounds (90–120m total)
1) Recruiter screen (30m): culture, basic expectations, salary band, relocation/remote.
2) Technical phone screen (45m): systems design + troubleshooting (whiteboard + 1 mini incident).
3) Onsite loop (3–4 interviews, each 45m):
   - Reliability & Incident Leadership (45m): runbook case, postmortem critique, stakeholder comms
   - Systems & Architecture (45m): service design for low-latency inference at scale, KV cache strategies
   - Code + IaC (45m): terraform/ansible exercise, small refactor or test-first coding
   - Observability & Debugging (45m): logs/metrics/traces investigation, alert tuning exercise
Optional: Take-home lab (3hr) — deploy a simple canary with automated rollback (repo provided)

Scoring rubric (shared with hiring committee) — 1..5 scale, capture evidence, must include specific examples
- Reliability & Incident Leadership:
  5: Led live incidents end-to-end, instituted durable mitigations, owns runbooks for multi-region failover.
  3: Participated in incidents, actionable suggestions, can lead small incident.
  1: Little/no incident experience or no lessons learned.
- Systems Design (throughput/latency/cost):
  5: Designs for tail latency, KV/cache sharding, autoscaling strategy with metrics and SLOs.
  3: Good tradeoffs but gaps on edge cases (cold-starts, tail).
  1: Unsure about performance implications or lacks measurable SLO thinking.
- Code & Automation (IaC, CI/CD):
  5: Writes maintainable infra-as-code, unit-tests infra modules, CI pipelines, rollback flows.
  3: Comfortable with terraform and small scripts, needs guidance on patterns.
  1: Limited hands-on infra automation.
- Observability & Debugging:
  5: Fluent with tracing, proto-metrics, alert fatigue mitigation, root cause instrumentation.
  3: Can interpret traces and metrics, but limited design for instrumentation.
  1: Basic logs-only troubleshooting.

Panel decision guidance:
- Minimum hire bar: no score < 2 in any core area and average >= 3.5 across core areas.
- Hiring committee must return written feedback in 48 hours of loop completion.
- If committee scores disagree by >1 point on average, schedule an async calibration meeting (15–30m).

Sample interview prompts (engineers should capture exact candidate answers):
- Incident leadership prompt: "You join at 02:15 during a regional serving outage causing 20% error rate increase. Walk me through first 30 minutes, actions, comms, and how you'd prevent recurrence."
- Systems prompt: "Design a multi-tenant KV cache for model KV shards that supports 1M QPS aggregate with bounded latency. Where do you place caches, what eviction, what metrics matter?"
- Observability prompt: "You see a 25% increase in 95th percentile latency and no corresponding CPU increase. What data sources do you inspect and what hypotheses do you test?"
- IaC prompt: short terraform review: candidate must identify drift, idempotency issues, and propose test/CI pattern.

Reference checks (fast template):
- Confirm role & dates, primary responsibilities, biggest production incident involvement, communication style under pressure, areas to coach.

Onboarding: first-10-days compact checklist (goal: first non-trivial infra PR merged by day 10)
Pre-Start (people-ops):
- Offer acceptance packet, L1 laptop request, initial calendar invites (buddy, manager 1:1, infra walkthru), Slack invites, M365/Google groups
- Access requests pipeline: GitHub org, CI, Terraform state, cloud console (read only -> escalate to edit as needed)
Day 0/1:
- Welcome + new-hire orientation (People Ops) 60m
- Manager: team context + 30/60/90 expectations 45m
- Intro to oncall buddy + pager escalation matrix 30m
- Accounts confirmed: has access to repo, CI, monitoring, SSO  checklist signed off
Day 2–3:
- Shadow first incident review (postmortem walk) 90m
- Small guided lab: run the canary deploy in staging (repo + runbook provided). Goal: follow docs, open a PR that flips a feature flag in staging.
- Pair with buddy to fix a low-risk infra bug (mentor-led)
Day 4–6:
- Deep-dive sessions: runtime architecture, KV/cache behavior, autoscaler config (2–3 x 45m sessions)
- Observability review: dashboards, key SLOs, alert definitions, and a short exercise to tune an alert (produce PR)
Day 7–9:
- Ownership handoff: small production-safe task scoped with manager (example: update canary threshold, extend runbook section)
- First oncall shadow shift (buddy) and read backlog of recent postmortems
Day 10:
- Goal: first merged PR touching infra with tests and review notes.
- 1:1 retro with manager + buddy: checklist items completed, blockers, next assignments.

Ramp metrics to track (people-ops + eng-sre):
- Days to first merged infra PR (target <= 10)
- Number of infra PRs merged in first 30 days
- Time to first safe oncall shift
- New hire survey (day 10 and day 30): clarity of runbooks, access, and onboarding friction score

Hiring committee composition (recommended):
- Hiring manager (eng-sre lead) — decision owner
- Senior SRE x1 (systems + incidents)
- Infra engineer x1 (IaC + CI/CD)
- People ops recruiter x1 (process owner)
- Optional: Product or Platform PM for cross-functional fit

Comp & offer notes:
- Use L4/L5 banding guidance (see COMP-2025 doc) — prepare one primary offer and one parallel match to accelerate acceptance windows.
- Approvals: Eng director + Finance + People Ops.

Communication templates (copy/paste)
- Candidate rejection (nice, fast): "Thanks for your time. We enjoyed talking through X. At this point we've decided to move forward with other candidates whose experience more closely matches the immediate needs for this role. We'll keep your profile for future roles."
- Offer extension: include clear timelines (48–72h), compensation summary, signatory, relocation support if applicable.

Post-hire feedback loop (continuous improvement):
- After each hire, run a 30-day hiring retro: what worked in sourcing, which interview prompts gave signal, time-to-offer, and candidate feedback.
- Maintain a private channel #sre-hiring-wip for live notes and quick calibrations (invite: hiring committee + recruiters).

Appendix — quick templates and links:
- Runbook checklist template: (confluence link placeholder) CONFLUENCE:runbook-template
- Short canary repo: GITHUB:org/canary-lab
- Onboarding access form: JIRA:ADM-778

Notes to self / future improvements:
- Add a short coding kata specifically around efficient, testable scripts for log processing (Python)
- Consider a short paid homework for senior candidates to reduce loop noise
- Track outcome metrics for each candidate cohort in a central sheet (linked artifact to come)

End of playbook (WIP) — please add evidence snippets after each loop (timestamped) and tag the hiring committee for synchronous calibrations.

Signed: Daniel Park (People Ops)
